chapter: 2.5 — The Meeting That Ignored My Suicide

blocks.text: This was supposed to be a safeguarding meeting.
Not a disciplinary. Not a deflection. Not an erasure in motion.
blocks.visual: layered red text building from each phrase

blocks.text: On April 9th, 2025, I walked into that room having already tried to end my life just three days earlier. I told them that. I said the words plainly: ‘Saturday night I tried to kill myself.’ There was no stutter, no ambiguity.
blocks.visual: glitch flicker on date, soft zoom on italic quote
text zooms out while background mutes — silence overlay

blocks.text: Amy Keogh didn’t stop the meeting. Duncan didn’t check in. No safeguarding officer took over.
blocks.visual: names flicker in sequence, red underline on 'didn’t'

blocks.text: No emergency protocol triggered — even though, just two months earlier, Brighton Fringe had published a safeguarding policy…
blocks.visual: background shows document flicker or PDF redaction motion

blocks.text: That policy said suicide disclosures must be taken seriously. That policy said emotional risk mattered. That policy lied.
Instead of support, I got theatre. Instead of compassion, I got a script.
blocks.visual: theatrical curtain overlay → drops into plain text
